newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cordoba province eyes $200 mln debt issue next yr.
newsitem.headline: Cordoba province eyes $200 mln debt issue next yr.

text.p: The Argentine province of Cordoba is waiting for Standard & Poor's to rate its creditworthiness so it can sell $200 million in debt on world markets next year, the province's governor said Tuesday.
"As soon as we get our rating, we're going to move forward," said Gov. Ramon Mestre, who is visiting Brazil at the head of a business delegation.
He told reporters the rating is expected to be granted in March, after which the province would hire a U.S. bank to act as lead manager in the debt issue.
The province has not decided if it will launch a Eurobond, Yankee bond or another kind of instrument, Mestre said.
"Let's see what the rating agency says first," he said.
The money raised in the issue would go to finance road, water, sewer, flood control and other infrastructure projects, Mestre said.
